newsitem.title: UK: Oil prices surge ahead of weekly U.S. stock data.
newsitem.headline: Oil prices surge ahead of weekly U.S. stock data.

text.p: World oil prices strengthened on Tuesday in a jumpy market ahead of crucial American Petroleum Institute (API) U.S. oil stock data.
International bellwether North Sea Brent blend crude for June loading closed 34 cents higher at $18.60 a barrel at 1955 GMT.
Traders attributed the initial rise to a rumour, later quashed, of a production hiccup at a large U.S. refinery.
"It just goes to show how supply-nervous this market is," said Charles Gray, oil analyst at Prudential Bache in London. "The tiniest hint that supply is under threat and the market takes off."
Traders said the market was keenly awaiting API oil stock data due to be released late on Tuesday.
In the week ended April 18, the data showed that U.S. crude oil stocks rose 1.38 million to 312.79 million barrels.
"Roll on the APIs to give the markets some meaningful fundamental news to trade with," said Leslie Nicholas, at commodity brokers GNI in London, lammenting the directionless state of the market.
Traders continued to monitor the situation in Nigeria, where ethnic clashes over the past few days have dogged Royal Dutch Shell Group's operations.
Concerns about Nigerian crude exports receded on Monday with the company's announcement on Monday that it had resumed full operations of its Forcados crude, but loadings were still delayed.
